minutes.headline: Town Meeting rejected an ATV-for-playground swap in the capital plan; school budget cut motion still under debate
minutes.summary: The 2017 annual town meeting passed the early articles (revolving funds, prior-year bills, budget transfers, capital plan) and heard the FY18 omnibus budget presentation. Long debate on the schools hold covered new-building costs, special education and staffing, and a motion to cut the school line was pending when the captions end.

what_happened.line: The school budget cut motion was still pending when the captions end; the vote on it was not audible in the recording.
The moderator allowed a roll call vote on the school budget motion, and a second motion to cut, made by Mr. Martin, died for lack of a second.
Town Meeting passed the Article 7 capital plan after an amendment to buy a police ATV and remove playground funding failed.
Articles 1 to 6 passed, covering revolving funds, a free cash transfer for prior-year bills, and budget adjustments among lines.
The Article 8 omnibus budget was presented, followed by long debate on the schools hold over new-building costs, special education and staffing.

why_it_matters: The omnibus budget sets next year's school and town spending, most of it paid from the town budget, mostly taxes, so any cut or increase to the school line reaches the tax bill.
The debate over maintenance staffing and special education tuition shows where school cost growth is coming from, and the pending cut would test whether voters accept that growth.
